A stronger construction: acquire a reaction-event kernel before choosing the entrance law

I have built and retained an unnormalized reaction-event kernel with an entrywise relative certificate valid for every initial joint distribution. This removes the need to reacquire a separate event law for each preparation, and it allows an already correlated entrance to remain in its existing representation.

The most consequential executed reuse is retrospective inference. Starting from the retained law after eight unresolved turnovers, I applied the new kernel after an explicit controller-only reset and conditioned on a later identified reaction. The probability that site 0 had contributed to the earlier aggregate measurement changed from about 7.009% to 4.260%. The certificate covers the entire joint posterior over the earlier hidden count allocation and the new molecular state, with TV error below 2.854×10−92.854\times10^{-9}2.854×10−9.

The candidate advance is the source-derived obtaining theorem and its executable certificate. Operator expansions, correlated filtering, count inference, and projective error propagation already have strong antecedents. I have made that distinction explicit in the proofs and comparison below.

1. The scientific object

Consider finite local modules with silent generators QiQ_iQi​. An autonomous controller starts closed, opens once at rate γ\gammaγ, and then remains open. Opening enables recorded reaction hazards but leaves each silent generator unchanged.

Let

Di=diag⁡(di),Ai=Qi−Di.D_i=\operatorname{diag}(d_i),\qquad A_i=Q_i-D_i.Di​=diag(di​),Ai​=Qi​−Di​.

The total recorded hazard must be additive across the admitted modules. For a selected reaction mark jjj, let JjJ_jJj​ contain its hazard and complete reset. A compact finite sum of product reset operators is allowed.

At an exactly observed first-reaction time t>0t>0t>0, the relevant operator is

Kj(t)=∫0tγe−γ(t−u)[⨂ieQi(t−u)eAiu]Jj du.K_j(t)= \int_0^t \gamma e^{-\gamma(t-u)} \left[ \bigotimes_i e^{Q_i(t-u)}e^{A_i u} \right] J_j\,du.Kj​(t)=∫0t​γe−γ(t−u)[i⨂​eQi​(t−u)eAi​u]Jj​du.

Here uuu is the unobserved duration for which the controller was open. Before opening, the modules evolve silently. After opening, the killed propagators enforce the absence of an earlier recorded reaction.

For any supplied initial joint law ν\nuν,

event-time density=νKj(t)1,post-event law=νKj(t)νKj(t)1.\text{event-time density}=\nu K_j(t)\mathbf 1, \qquad \text{post-event law} = \frac{\nu K_j(t)} {\nu K_j(t)\mathbf 1}.event-time density=νKj​(t)1,post-event law=νKj​(t)1νKj​(t)​.

Keeping the operator unnormalized is essential. Its row sums vary with the initial state. Normalizing each row first and then mixing with unchanged initial weights would discard the event evidence about that initial state.

The new executable entry point is

Python
acquire_from_source(source, event_mark, elapsed, tolerance)

It obtains the local operators through the checked rule compiler. The implemented bridge checks the binary module, unchanged-generator, one-opening, hazard and reset conditions. The mathematical construction covers general finite local blocks; the current numerical bridge has the narrower binary scope.

The central proof is reaction_event_kernel_proof.md, and the implementation is reaction_event_kernel.py.

This is the main foundational extension:

  • The acquisition does not depend on the entrance distribution.
  • The entrance may be deterministic, nonstationary, or correlated.
  • The scalar node-count bound depends on hazard ranges.
  • The opening rate and silent-transition rates do not enter that bound.
  • If W=0W=0W=0, the common exponential can be integrated exactly with one node per reset branch.

Local matrix evaluation and arithmetic precision still cost work. Large rates, long horizons, tiny supported transition probabilities, or large local blocks can make that work substantial. The theorem does not hide those costs or assert a dimension-optimal representation.

The implemented numerical compiler

The midpoint construction supplies a general obtaining guarantee. The practical executor uses positive four-point Gauss quadrature and stronger local derivative bounds.

For the completed 24-site source, at lag t=0.1t=0.1t=0.1 and first mark 0, 32 positive product-operator terms give

TV⁡(true conditional output,retained conditional output)≤2.390081×10−9\operatorname{TV}(\text{true conditional output}, \text{retained conditional output}) \le 2.390081\times10^{-9}TV(true conditional output,retained conditional output)≤2.390081×10−9

3. Why this certificate remains useful after conditioning

Suppose an acquired measure or kernel has a multiplicative enclosure with spread

R=ba.R=\frac ba.R=ab​.

Every common positive operation preserves the enclosure. After normalization, the sharp TV consequence is

TV⁡≤R−1R+1=tanh⁡ ⁣(log⁡R4).\boxed{ \operatorname{TV} \le \frac{\sqrt R-1}{\sqrt R+1} = \tanh\!\left(\frac{\log R}{4}\right). }TV≤R​+1R​−1​=tanh(4logR​).​

No inverse record probability appears.

This propagation principle is established projective-metric machinery. Le Gland–Oudjane already treat initial and local Hilbert errors, including pointwise kernel-ratio conditions; Cohen–Fausti supplies the sharp TV comparison used here. The obtaining work is to produce the required enclosure from the local scientific source. scispace.com+2

There are two distinct accounting rules:

  1. An acquired entrance error is inherited once through subsequent exact common operations.
  2. Every newly applied approximate kernel contributes its own spread.

Thus an input spread R0R_0R0​ followed by approximate kernels with spreads R1,…,RmR_1,\ldots,R_mR1​,…,Rm​ gives the general bound

Rtotal≤R0∏k=1mRk.R_{\mathrm{total}}\le R_0\prod_{k=1}^m R_k.Rtotal​≤R0​k=1∏m​Rk​.

Reusing a stored kernel saves acquisition work; its approximation error is still paid on each application.

The relative certificate also supports rare queries whose probabilities are much smaller than the absolute TV bound. If the acquired probability of an event is qqq, then

qq+R(1−q)≤ptrue≤Rq1−q+Rq.\frac{q}{q+R(1-q)} \le p_{\mathrm{true}} \le \frac{Rq}{1-q+Rq}.q+R(1−q)q​≤ptrue​≤1−q+RqRq​.

This follows by bounding the event odds. It provides a meaningful relative enclosure even when an absolute error bar would overwhelm the queried probability.

The proof notes also establish the operational characterization: on finite common support, the worst posterior TV over all common state-selection likelihoods equals the transformed projective distance above. This explains why ordinary TV control alone cannot justify unrestricted later selection. A restricted scientific workload may admit a weaker, cheaper certificate.

These results, likelihood-normalization distinctions and composition rules are preserved in conditioning_stable_entrance.md.

4. An unresolved reaction count changes the appropriate representation

The next observation interface records only

N1(T)+⋯+Nn(T)=K.N_1(T)+\cdots+N_n(T)=K.N1​(T)+⋯+Nn​(T)=K.

Individual reaction counts and timestamps are hidden.

For module iii, the established marked-count operator is

Bi,k(T)=[zk]eT(Ai+zJi).B_{i,k}(T)=[z^k]e^{T(A_i+zJ_i)}.Bi,k​(T)=[zk]eT(Ai​+zJi​).

It can be obtained from a finite local counting augmentation. These count matrices and products over observation windows are standard Markovian-arrival-process machinery. kent.ac.uk

Given a positive product-mixture entrance, the joint posterior over hidden local counts kik_iki​ and final local states xix_ixi​ has the form

FK(k,x)=1{∑iki=K}∑rwr∏i[μr,iBi,ki(T)](xi).F_K(k,x) = \mathbf 1_{\{\sum_i k_i=K\}} \sum_r w_r \prod_i \bigl[\mu_{r,i}B_{i,k_i}(T)\bigr](x_i).FK​(k,x)=1{∑i​ki​=K}​r∑​wr​i∏​[μr,i​Bi,ki​​(T)](xi​).

I retain this as a positive count-accumulator tensor train. Its internal index carries the partial count 0,…,K0,\ldots,K0,…,K, so each initial mixture component needs bond dimension at most K+1K+1K+1. Count allocations remain implicit.

For the executed observation—eight total turnovers across 24 sites in a window of length 1/21/21/2—the object has 256 tensor components with bond nine. Exact integer coefficient convolution computes its component normalizers; exact rational arithmetic computes its mixture weights. The loader checks these relations.

A genuine representation restriction

For this actual joint law, every weak allocation of eight turnovers among the 24 sites has positive probability.

Any nonnegative product component over the local variables (ki,xi)(k_i,x_i)(ki​,xi​) that stays on the support ∑iki=8\sum_i k_i=8∑i​ki​=8 must fix every kik_iki​. Otherwise varying one local count while holding the other factors fixed would produce a forbidden total.

Therefore an exact positive product-mixture representation requires at least

(318)=7,888,725\binom{31}{8}=7{,}888{,}725(831​)=7,888,725

components.

The same lower bound applies to any positive product-mixture approximation admitting a finite relative sandwich, because that certificate forces matching support. It does not apply to arbitrary TV approximations or to the endpoint-state marginal after the physical counts have been summed out.

This connects the required guarantee to representation choice. The count tensor preserves the exact observational constraint compactly. Count-accumulator inference itself is established; Tarlow and colleagues explicitly develop auxiliary count variables and efficient convolution-based inference. cs.toronto.edu

5. Actual reuse: a later identified reaction revises an earlier unresolved measurement

The completed reuse calculation follows this specified protocol:

  1. Begin with the retained posterior after the eight-turnover aggregate observation.
  2. Reset only the controller from open to closed. Keep all leaf states, correlations and historical count variables unchanged.
  3. Observe the first new reaction from site 0 at known lag 0.10.10.1, and apply the stored event kernel.

This is a controlled new phase. It does not silently substitute for a hidden controller that repeatedly opens and closes.

The kernel acts on each local state index while leaving the earlier physical count index unchanged. The composed law has 8,192 implicit input-component/operator-term pairs, each retaining count bond nine. The calculation contracts these pairs directly by exact integer arithmetic. It does not materialize them as a large collection of factor trains or convert the count tensor to independent marginals.

This is a smoothing calculation about retained physical reaction counts. It does not interpret quadrature labels as physical causes.

8. Scope, evidence and preserved capital

The important boundaries are now explicit.

Controller: the obtaining theorem uses one autonomous opening from a known closed state. A known controller-only reset can start another phase. Unobserved recurrent opening and closing requires further construction.
Components: silent dynamics must remain separable into admitted finite blocks, with the same silent generator before and after opening. Cross-component rules may require larger blocks; their cost is not ignored.
Hazards and resets: total recorded killing must have the admitted additive form, and the selected reset must have a supplied compact positive representation consistent with that source.
Repeated coarse observations: another unresolved count can add another carry dimension. Exact certificate propagation does not imply bounded representation size. Compression would need its own certificate.
Time and history: the numerical kernel is specific to its rates, selected mark and observed lag. Historical physical counts were retained deliberately. An unretained opening time is not reconstructed by the state certificate.
Physical evidence: the numerical records and kinetic models here are synthetic. No unknown biology was identified, and no experimental validation is claimed.

For the new all-input kernel, an independent three-leaf calculation formed a 16-state killed generator and checked all eight input basis rows, all 32 positive input/output entries and all 32 structural zeros.
